claims.title: Which complex structures correspond to positive lines?
claims.hypotheses: A complex Hermitian space of signature (1,n−1), a choice s=±1 and t=si. At the remaining places of the unitary datum the corresponding form is negative definite.
claims.statement: The positive lines are in bijection with the complex-linear endomorphisms J satisfying J²=−I, preserving the Hermitian pairing and making Re(−t h(Jx,x)) positive on every nonzero x. The t-eigenspace is the line and J=t(2P−I) for its Hermitian projection P. At a negative-definite place J is multiplication by −t.

claims.title: When do two rational periods give the same positive line?
claims.hypotheses: The linked unitary datum has a=m=1, one infinite place of positive index one, all designated embeddings equal to τ₀, and a compatible action of the order on ℂᵍ with the prescribed embedding multiplicities. The rational polarised form is equivalent to the standard form at infinity.
claims.statement: Rational periods for the fixed form modulo complex-linear target isomorphisms correspond to its positive lines at the distinguished place. Transport by Q′(γw)=Q(w) sends the line to γᵥℓ for a rational similitude of positive multiplier.
